author: Max
summary: A wire-style rundown of Tuesday night's action around the NBA, featuring Sensabaugh's 40-point eruption for Utah, a last-second Timberwolves win in Portland, and Detroit's upset of red-hot San Antonio.

content.value:
## Brice Sensabaugh scores 40 points and leads huge 4th quarter as Jazz beat Clippers for 2nd win

The Utah Jazz finally have something to celebrate. Brice Sensabaugh erupted for a season-high 40 points, pouring in 25 of them in the fourth quarter alone, as the Jazz pulled away from the Los Angeles Clippers 132-107 on Tuesday night. The victory marks just the second win of the season for Utah, which has struggled mightily out of the gate. Sensabaugh's fourth-quarter explosion turned what had been a competitive game into a rout, giving the Jazz their most lopsided victory of the young campaign. For a team starving for positive momentum, the second-year wing's breakout performance couldn't have come at a better time.

## McDaniels scores with 2.6 seconds left to lift Timberwolves to 106-105 win over Trail Blazers

Jaden McDaniels played the hero in Portland on Tuesday night, converting a go-ahead layup with just 2.6 seconds remaining to lift the Minnesota Timberwolves to a 106-105 victory over the Trail Blazers. The winning sequence came after Minnesota forced a turnover on a Portland inbounds pass, giving McDaniels the opportunity to cap the comeback. The Timberwolves had clawed their way back from a deficit to set up the dramatic finish, and McDaniels delivered when it mattered most. It's the kind of clutch play that defines tight road wins, and Minnesota escaped the Pacific Northwest with two crucial points in the standings.

## Cunningham, Jenkins lead surge as Pistons snap Spurs' 12-game winning streak with 105-93 victory

The San Antonio Spurs' impressive run came to an end in Detroit on Tuesday night. Cade Cunningham scored 27 points and Daniss Jenkins added 25, with 21 of those coming in a dominant second half, as the Pistons toppled the Spurs 105-93 and snapped San Antonio's 12-game winning streak. The Spurs had been one of the league's hottest teams, riding a surge that had vaulted them up the Western Conference standings, but Detroit's balanced attack and Jenkins' second-half takeover proved too much to handle. For the Pistons, it's a statement win over a team that had looked nearly unstoppable in recent weeks.
